issues.title: Remote links on issues
issues.body:
## User story

As an Armature user, I want to see which external documentation pages reference an issue, so that I can jump from the work item to its spec. The first consumer is Stator (praetorianer777/Stator#32).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Migration adds `issue_remote_link` (org, issue, url, title, source application, icon url, created by, created at) with the usual tenant-isolation RLS policy; unique on (issue, url)
- [ ] `GET/POST /api/v1/issues/{issueKey}/remote-links` and `DELETE /api/v1/issues/{issueKey}/remote-links/{id}`, in the route table, so they appear in `api/openapi.json` and as MCP tools
- [ ] POST with an existing URL updates the title instead of duplicating (idempotent sync)
- [ ] Only users who can edit the issue can add or remove links; read-only tokens are refused
- [ ] Issue view shows a "Pages" section listing the links with source icon and title
- [ ] `issue.updated` is not emitted for remote-link changes; a new `issue.remote_link.added|removed` topic is

## Tests

Unit tests for validation, integration tests including a raw-SQL RLS attempt, and an e2e scenario that adds a link via the API and sees it on the issue view.

issues.title: Documentation link in the project sidebar
issues.body:
## User story

As a team using Armature together with a documentation tool, I want a project to link to its documentation space, so that the docs are one click away from the board.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Project settings accept an optional documentation URL and label
- [ ] When set, the project sidebar shows a "Docs" entry opening that URL
- [ ] Exposed on the project resource in the API so tools like Stator can set it (praetorianer777/Stator#83)

## Tests

Unit and integration tests for the setting, e2e scenario for the sidebar entry.

issues.title: Version the application with semantic versioning
issues.body:
## User story

As someone deploying Armature, I want every build to carry a semantic version and every release to be a tag, so that I know which version runs, can pin the chart to it and can read what changed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A `VERSION` file at the repository root is the single source of truth, starting at `0.1.0`
- [ ] `make release VERSION=x.y.z` refuses unless on a clean `main` with a valid semver greater than the current one, then writes `VERSION`, `web/package.json` and `Chart.yaml` (`version` and `appVersion`), moves `## Unreleased` in `CHANGELOG.md` under the new version, regenerates the chart golden files, commits `Release x.y.z` and tags `vx.y.z` (no push)
- [ ] The backend image reports `x.y.z` on a tag, `x.y.z+<n>.g<sha>` past one, and `<VERSION>+dev` with no tag; `buildinfo` strips a leading `v`
- [ ] The Jenkinsfile tags images without the `v` so they match the chart's `appVersion`, passes the version build args, and no longer overwrites `latest` from branch builds
- [ ] `api/openapi.json` `info.version` stays the API contract number; the split is recorded in `docs/decisions.md`
- [ ] README gains a "Releasing" section; `CHANGELOG.md` exists

## Tests

A unit test refuses a `VERSION`, `web/package.json` and `Chart.yaml` that disagree. The release script is exercised against a scratch clone.

issues.title: Holiday calendars and working weeks
issues.body:
## User story

As an organization administrator with people in several countries, I want named holiday calendars and a working week per person, so that planning knows which days somebody can work.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Migration adds `holiday_calendar` (one default per organization), `holiday` (day, name, half day) and `member_schedule` (person, calendar or the default, minutes per weekday), with the usual tenant-isolation RLS and CHECKs mirroring the service's validation
- [ ] `member_schedule` admits only non-customer members of the organization, enforced by a trigger
- [ ] `GET/POST /holiday-calendars`, `GET/PATCH/DELETE /holiday-calendars/{calendarID}`, `PUT .../days`, `POST .../import` (an `.ics` file, recurring events refused with a sentence) and `GET/PUT /users/{userID}/schedule`, in the route table, so they appear in `api/openapi.json` and as MCP tools
- [ ] Only organization administrators change calendars and other people's schedules; a person can read their own
- [ ] A settings page "Holidays" lists, edits and imports calendars; the users page sets a person's working week and calendar; the profile shows it read-only
- [ ] Every new organization gets an empty default calendar; the demo seed fills it with a few days

## Tests

Unit tests for the day arithmetic and the `.ics` parser, integration tests including raw-SQL RLS and guard attempts, and an e2e scenario that imports an `.ics` and sees the days.

issues.title: People record their absences
issues.body:
## User story

As a team member, I want to record when I am away, so that my colleagues and the plan stop counting on me for those days, without anyone learning why.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Migration adds `absence` (person, first day, last day, half day, created by) with no reason or note column; overlapping absences of one person are refused by the database
- [ ] `GET /absences`, `POST /absences`, `PATCH/DELETE /absences/{absenceID}`, in the route table
- [ ] A person records their own absences; an organization administrator, or a scrum master or project administrator of a team the person belongs to, may record them for that person; anyone else is refused
- [ ] Colleagues see only that the person is away; customers never see absences
- [ ] The profile page has an "Absences" section; the teams page lets a lead record one for a member
- [ ] `docs/privacy.md` and the privacy service cover absences: purpose, what is held, export, erasure, member removal and a retention window (`ARMATURE_RETAIN_ABSENCES`)

## Tests

Unit tests for validation, integration tests for every role case and a raw-SQL overlap and RLS attempt, vitest for the profile section, and an e2e scenario recording an absence.

Depends on #28.

issues.title: Holidays and absences on the calendar and in capacity
issues.body:
## User story

As a project member, I want holidays and my colleagues' absences on the calendar and taken out of capacity, so that the plan reflects who can actually work.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One availability service combines working weeks, holiday calendars and absences into minutes available per person per day
- [ ] The project calendar shows holidays (shaded like weekends, with their name) and absences (the person and "away"), with a toggle to hide them
- [ ] The timeline shades the organization's default holidays
- [ ] Team load spreads estimates over working days only and scales each team's weekly capacity by its members' availability; the decision on team capacity is updated
- [ ] Sprint planning shows the team's available hours in the sprint window as a hint; capacity still warns and never refuses

## Tests

Unit tests for the availability service and the changed load spreading, integration tests for the calendar and plan responses, vitest for the month grid, and an e2e scenario where an absence appears on the project calendar.

Depends on #28 and #29.

issues.title: Resource planning per project: teams for scrum, teams or people for kanban
issues.body:
## User story

As a project lead, I want a resource planning view that sets the work scheduled against the hours available per week, by team for a scrum project and by team or by person for a kanban project, so that I see who is overloaded before it happens.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Projects gain a planning method (`scrum` or `kanban`, backfilled from their boards, new projects from their template) and a resource grouping (`team` or `person`); the database refuses grouping by person on a scrum project
- [ ] Project settings choose the method and, for kanban, the grouping
- [ ] A new project feature "Resources" adds a sidebar page
- [ ] `GET /projects/{projectKey}/resources?from&to`, in the route table, returns per row (team or person) and per week the capacity in hours, the load in hours, the contributing issues and the days away
- [ ] Load is an issue's remaining time (or its estimate) spread over the row's working days between start and due; unscheduled and unestimated work is listed, not guessed
- [ ] Rows over capacity carry an `over-allocated` warning; nothing is refused
- [ ] The page draws a row per team or person and a column per week, holidays and absences hatched, and lists the issues of a week on click

## Tests

Unit tests for grouping and spreading, integration tests including the raw-SQL scrum guard and refusals, vitest for the page, and e2e scenarios for a kanban project switching to people and a scrum project offering only teams.

Depends on #30.

issues.title: A team manager can change any member's absences by adding them to a team
issues.body:
## User story

As a member of an organization, I want only my own team's managers to be able to change my absences, so that someone who simply adds me to a team cannot rewrite the days I am away.

## What happens today

`mayRecord` in `backend/internal/availability/absence_service.go` lets someone record, change or delete a person's absences in three cases:
- they are that person;
- they hold `org.administer`;
- they hold `team.manage` in a project where that person is on a team.

A team manager also decides who is on their teams: `POST /teams/{teamID}/members` accepts any non-customer member of the organization. So a scrum master of any project can take over anybody's absences in two requests:

1. `POST /api/v1/teams/{theirTeam}/members {"userId": "<anyone, an org admin included>"}`
2. `POST /api/v1/absences {"userId": ...}`, or `PATCH` / `DELETE /api/v1/absences/{id}` with an id from `GET /absences`.

The impact is limited to planning data. No reason is stored, nothing becomes readable that was not already, and both steps land in the audit log. It is still a way around the rule the feature was built on (#29): only the person, an administrator or *their* team's manager.

Found in the security review of #32 and #37 (confidence 4/10, below the bar for a vulnerability).

## Acceptance criteria

A check on team membership alone cannot close this. The manager controls the team, so "was on the team before this request" only means waiting a minute, and project read access comes from org-wide roles too. The fix limits what a manager may do and makes it visible:

- [ ] A team manager may record an absence for a member of their team, but may change or delete only absences they recorded themselves (`created_by`). The person's own entries, and an administrator's, are out of a manager's reach.
- [ ] When someone other than the person records, changes or removes their absence, the person is told through the inbox (and mail, if they asked for it), without the dates in the mail.
- [ ] An administrator and the person themselves are unaffected.
- [ ] A refusal is a 403 with a sentence that names who to ask instead, for example "Only Ada or an administrator can change this absence."
- [ ] The rule is written in `docs/decisions.md` next to "An absence says when, never why, and nobody approves it", and `docs/privacy.md` says accurately who may change someone's absences.

## Tests

- **Integration:**
  - a scrum master cannot change or delete an absence the person or an administrator recorded;
  - a scrum master can still change one they recorded;
  - the person gets an inbox entry each time someone else touches their absences;
  - the person and an administrator keep full control.
- **Proven in SQL as well:** if the rule moves into the database, prove it there too, as CLAUDE.md asks.
- **Browser:** the person sees the notice in their inbox after a scrum master records an absence for them.

issues.title: Say what share of a person's week belongs to a project, so people on two projects are not counted twice
issues.body:
## User story

As a kanban lead, I want to say that Bob gives half his week to this project, so that the resources page measures his work here against 20 h and not the 40 h his week holds.

## What happens today

Person and team rows take their capacity from the whole working week (`hoursOfWeek` with `peopleTime`, `plan/resources.go:208, 266-270`; `workdays.go:98-125`). The availability tables hold a week and absences (migrations `00909`, `00910`). Nothing stores how a person's week is split between projects.

So Bob, who works half on A and half on B, shows 40 h available in both. Neither project warns, even when he carries 30 h in each.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A project administrator can set a share (a percentage, 100 by default) per person for the project, and per team member for team rows.
- [ ] Capacity and nominal hours on the resources page are scaled by the share. The tooltip says so, for example "20 of 20 h (50% of the week)".
- [ ] The total of a person's shares across projects is shown where it is set. Going over 100% warns and never refuses, like capacity elsewhere.
- [ ] The share is in `docs/decisions.md` next to "Resource planning is in hours; team capacity stays in points".

## Tests

- **Unit:** the scaled capacity, and a share of 0.
- **Integration:**
  - setting and reading the share;
  - the refusal for someone without project administration;
  - the resources response with a share, contract-validated.
- **Vitest:** the share editor and the tooltip.
- **Browser:** setting 50% halves a person's week on the page.

issues.title: Carry a holiday calendar's fixed-date holidays into the next year
issues.body:
## User story

As an administrator, I want New Year, 1 May and Christmas to carry into next year, so that I do not have to type or import every calendar again each January, and the plan does not quietly count those days as working days.

## What happens today

A holiday is one dated row (`migrations/00909_holiday_calendars.sql:28-40`). There is no recurrence and no copy endpoint (`routes_organization.go:81-92`), and `CalendarDays.tsx` offers only "Add a day" and "Import .ics". The decisions cover refusing RRULE in imports, not repeating fixed dates.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A "Copy to next year" action on a calendar proposes this year's days moved to the same dates next year, as an unsaved draft the administrator reviews. Movable feasts such as Easter are then corrected by hand or by import.
- [ ] Or a holiday can be marked "every year", stored as month and day and expanded when read. Pick one and write the choice in `docs/decisions.md` next to "Holidays are named calendars a person is given".
- [ ] Copying never overwrites a day the next year already holds.

## Tests

- **Unit:** the copy, including 29 February.
- **Integration:** the endpoint (success, refusal for a non-administrator), contract-validated.
- **Browser:** copy, review, save, and see next year's days on the calendar.

issues.title: Reach every unscheduled and unestimated issue from the resources page, not only the first 25
issues.body:
## User story

As a lead tidying up a plan, I want to open the whole list of work the resources page could not place, so that I can date and estimate it, not only the first 25.

## What happens today

`web/src/features/resources/UnplacedWork.tsx:24-44` cuts each list to `RESOURCE_LIST_LIMIT` (25, `config.ts:345`) and prints "and N more" as plain text. The backend already returns the full lists (`plan/resources.go:172-176`).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] "and N more" expands the list in place, or links to the issue search with the matching query (open issues in the project with no start or due date, or no estimate).
- [ ] If it links, the query is the same one the page uses, so the counts agree.

## Tests

- **Vitest:** the expand (or the link and its query) with 30 issues.

issues.title: Let finished work leave a kanban board, so the done lane and its WIP count stop growing forever
issues.body:
## User story

As a kanban team, I want work finished a while ago to leave the board, so that the Done column stays readable and the board loads quickly a year in.

## What happens today

With no sprint scope, `loadCards` (`backend/internal/board/service.go:354-370`) reads `WHERE i.project_id = $1 AND t.hierarchy_level >= $2`, with no status, `resolved_at` or row limit. `BoardView.tsx:250` counts `swimlane.cards.length` against the WIP limit.

After a year the Done column holds thousands of cards, the payload grows without bound, and a WIP limit on a lane holding a done status is always exceeded. The README says "kanban shows everything", and the plan already has the idea "Closed work leaves the plan after a number of days the reader chooses".

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A kanban board leaves out done-category issues resolved more than N days ago, N set per board (for example 14 by default, 0 meaning never).
- [ ] The board says how many finished issues it is leaving out, with a link to search for them.
- [ ] WIP limits count only what the board shows.
- [ ] The rule is written next to "A board is scoped by team, and its type is behaviour".

## Tests

- **Integration:** an issue resolved 30 days ago is not on a board set to 14 days; the setting is refused for a reader.
- **Browser:** the hidden count on a seeded board.

issues.title: Quick filters on a board: mine, by assignee, label, type or epic, and a text search
issues.body:
## User story

As someone working from a busy board, I want to narrow it to my cards or to one epic's, so that I can find my work without making a new board.

## What happens today

`web/src/features/board/BoardView.tsx` and `routes/board.tsx` have no filter controls. The only scope a board's cards have is team or sprint (`board/service.go` `cardScope`), which is stored with the board. Nothing narrows it for the moment.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Chips above the board: Only mine, Assignee, Label, Type, Epic, and a text box matching key and summary.
- [ ] They filter the cards already loaded, and say how many are hidden.
- [ ] The choice is kept in the URL, so a filtered board can be linked.
- [ ] WIP counts stay on the whole lane, and say so when filtered.

## Tests

- **Vitest:** each chip, the combination, and the URL round trip.
- **Browser:** Only mine on the seeded board.

issues.title: Customers can raise a new request by mailing the desk
issues.body:
## User story

As a customer, I want to mail support@ about a new problem and have it become a request, so that I do not have to find the portal first.

## What happens today

`desk/inbound.go:170-172`: a mail that names no request is recorded as Unmatched and answered with "use the portal". Nothing raises a request from mail. The decision "Replies come in by POP3" covers replies only.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A desk can name a default request type for mail. An unmatched mail that passes the sender's own server checks and the desk's trusted domains raises a request of that type, with the sender as reporter (a customer without a password, as followers already are). Its subject becomes the summary, its text the description, and its attachments the request's files.
- [ ] A desk without a mail request type keeps today's refusal.
- [ ] Auto-submitted mail never raises a request.
- [ ] The decision is extended to say when mail raises a request.

## Tests

- **Integration:**
  - a new mail raises a request with the right reporter and type;
  - an untrusted domain is refused;
  - an auto-reply is skipped;
  - a reply to an existing request is still a reply.
- **Browser:** the raised request in the customer's portal list.

issues.title: Send mail through an SMTP server that needs a login or implicit TLS
issues.body:
## User story

As an operator, I want Armature to send through SES, Microsoft 365, Gmail or my company's relay, so that I do not have to run an open relay next to it.

## What happens today

`mail/mail.go:72` calls `smtp.SendMail(m.Addr, nil, ...)` with no authentication. The only setting is `ARMATURE_SMTP_ADDR` (`config/config.go:72,193`). POP3 already has a user, a password and TLS, but SMTP has none.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `ARMATURE_SMTP_USER`, `ARMATURE_SMTP_PASSWORD` and `ARMATURE_SMTP_TLS` (`starttls`, `implicit` or `none`). PLAIN auth is used only over TLS.
- [ ] The password comes from a secret in the chart, and the README's environment table lists all three.
- [ ] A refused login is logged once with a sentence, and the outbox keeps the mail for retry.

## Tests

- **Integration:** against the stack's Mailpit with auth required, or a small SMTP test server: a send with the login succeeds, and one with a wrong password fails with the logged sentence.

issues.title: Let a desk's business calendar take its holidays from a holiday calendar
issues.body:
## User story

As a desk administrator, I want the SLA calendar to skip the same public holidays the organization already keeps, so that I maintain one list and the clocks agree with the plan.

## What happens today

`business_calendar.holidays` is a flat per-project list (`desk/calendar.go`), separate from the organization's holiday calendars (#28). The decision "Holidays are named calendars a person is given" names pointing the SLA calendar at a holiday calendar as later work.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A business calendar can name a holiday calendar. Its days (half days as half the day's hours) are skipped by the clocks, alongside or instead of the desk's own list.
- [ ] Deleting a holiday calendar a desk uses is refused with a sentence naming the desk, or falls back to the desk's own list. Decide which.
- [ ] Changing the holiday calendar's days takes effect for open clocks from then on.

## Tests

- **Unit:** working time across a holiday taken from the named calendar.
- **Integration:** setting the link, a refusal for a non-administrator, and the clocks across a holiday.

issues.title: Group a desk's customers into customer organizations who can see each other's requests
issues.body:
## User story

As a customer at Globex, I want to see the requests my colleagues raised with the desk, so that we do not each report the same outage. As an agent, I want to see which company a request comes from.

## What happens today

There is no table or code for customer organizations. A customer sees their own requests and those they follow. Trusted domains decide who may write, not who may read together.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A desk administrator can make customer organizations, add customers to them, and optionally add new customers by domain.
- [ ] A customer can choose to share a request with their organization when raising it, and can see the shared requests of their organization in the portal.
- [ ] Agents see the customer organization on the request, and queues and reports can filter by it.
- [ ] Internal notes stay invisible to every customer.
- [ ] The decisions and `docs/privacy.md` say who sees what.

## Tests

- **Integration:** sharing, visibility to a colleague, invisibility to another organization, notes still hidden, and RLS through raw SQL.
- **Browser:** a colleague sees the shared request in the portal.

issues.title: Search results and the project's issue list cannot be paged past the first 100
issues.body:
## User story

As someone working through a query that matches 450 issues, I want to page through all of them, so that the ones after the first 100 are not out of reach.

## What happens today

- `web/src/routes/search.tsx:29` calls `useIssues({ q, limit: SEARCH_PAGE_SIZE })` (100, `config.ts:140`) with no offset. `:70` says "N issues, the first 100 shown".
- `routes/project-detail.tsx:34,59` caps at `ISSUE_PAGE_SIZE` (100), while `:179` shows the full total, with nothing saying rows are missing.
- The API accepts `offset` (`httpapi/filter_handlers.go:172`), but no `.tsx` uses it.
- The CSV export is no way out either, while it is capped at 50 (#80).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both lists page (or load more) through `offset` and `total`, with the page kept in the URL.
- [ ] The project page says how many of the total are shown.
- [ ] Bulk selection says whether it covers the shown page or the whole result.

## Tests

- **Vitest:** paging controls and the URL.
- **Browser:** page to the second hundred of a seeded result.

issues.title: Bulk edit can move, delete, remove labels and set versions, components and fields
issues.body:
## User story

As a project administrator reorganising work, I want to move 80 issues to a new project, or strip a retired label from them, in one step and not 80.

## What happens today

- `bulk/bulk.go:22-32` `Input` holds only Priority, Assignee, SprintID, MilestoneID, TeamID, AddLabels and Transition.
- `web/src/features/filters/BulkBar.tsx` offers priority, assignee, add labels and a free-text transition name only. It does not offer the sprint, milestone and team changes the API supports.
- Move exists only one issue at a time (`POST /issues/{key}/move`).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Bulk input gains `moveTo` (project, with a status mapping), `removeLabels`, `fixVersions`, `components`, custom field values and `delete`. Each goes through the existing per-issue service calls, one transaction per issue.
- [ ] BulkBar offers sprint, milestone and team pickers, and picks the transition from the names the selected issues share.
- [ ] Delete confirms with the count and the noun ("Delete 80 issues").
- [ ] Each operation is checked against the caller's permissions per issue, and refused issues are listed with their reason.

## Tests

- **Integration:** each new operation, with a refusal per permission.
- **Vitest:** the new pickers.
- **Browser:** bulk-remove a label from a search result.

issues.title: Keep the api and web available through node drains and rollouts: disruption budgets and a shutdown drain
issues.body:
## User story

As an operator, I want a node drain or a rolling update to drop no requests, so that people do not see 502s every time I deploy.

## What happens today

There is no PodDisruptionBudget, `preStop`, `topologySpreadConstraints` or anti-affinity anywhere in `deploy/charts/armature`. `cmd/api/main.go:276-281` calls `srv.Shutdown` as soon as SIGTERM arrives. `/readyz` never turns unready first, so the listener closes while endpoints are still being removed.

**Scenario:** a node drain evicts both default api replicas, or both web replicas, at once. During a rolling update, requests still routed to a terminating pod get connection refused or 502.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Optional PDBs (`minAvailable: 1`) for api and web, on by default when replicas are more than one.
- [ ] Optional topology spread across nodes.
- [ ] On SIGTERM the api fails `/readyz`, waits a configurable drain delay, then shuts down gracefully. Web gets a `preStop` sleep.
- [ ] The README's deployment section describes them.

## Tests

- **Helm golden files:** updated for each setting.
- **Unit:** the api's shutdown order (readiness off, delay, then Shutdown).

issues.title: Self-service password recovery by mail
issues.body:
## User story

As someone who forgot my password, I want to reset it from the sign-in page by mail, so that I am not locked out when nobody can reset it for me.

## What happens today

Nothing in the backend or web handles a forgotten password. The only match for the idea is a seeded demo story (`cmd/seed/main.go:367`). An administrator's reset (`SetManagedPassword`) works only for people whose sole organization is the administrator's, as the decisions say. An owner, or someone in two organizations, has no way back.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] "Forgot your password?" on the sign-in page takes an address and always answers the same way, whether or not the address is known.
- [ ] A known address gets a single-use link, valid for an hour, stored hashed. It is rate limited per address and per IP.
- [ ] Using it sets a new password and ends every session and API token the person holds.
- [ ] Accounts that sign in only through a provider are told to use it.
- [ ] Each step is audited, and the decisions record the rule.

## Tests

- **Integration:**
  - request, use, reuse refused, expired refused;
  - sessions and tokens ended;
  - the same answer for an unknown address.
- **Browser:** reset through Mailpit and sign in.

issues.title: A second factor for password sign-in, and an organization setting that requires it
issues.body:
## User story

As the owner of a self-hosted tracker, I want administrators to need a second factor, so that a leaked password alone does not open the organization.

## What happens today

There is no TOTP, WebAuthn or passkey support anywhere in the code or docs. `auth/service.go:210` (`Login`) goes straight from the password to a session.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A person can enrol a TOTP app (QR code plus secret), confirm with a code, and get ten single-use recovery codes, shown once.
- [ ] Password sign-in asks for a code when enrolled, with its own rate limit.
- [ ] An organization can require a second factor for administrators, or for everyone. A session without one is held to enrolment.
- [ ] Single sign-on sessions rely on the provider's factor.
- [ ] Enrolment, removal and recovery-code use are audited, and the decisions record the rule.
- [ ] WebAuthn is noted as later work if not done here.

## Tests

- **Unit:** TOTP verification with clock skew.
- **Integration:** enrolment, sign-in with and without a code, recovery codes single use, and an organization's requirement.
- **Browser:** enrol and sign in.

issues.title: See your active sessions and sign out other devices
issues.body:
## User story

As someone who left a session open on a shared machine, I want to see where I am signed in and end the others, without changing my password. Single sign-on users have no password to change.

## What happens today

The router has no session routes. `user_session` keeps the user agent, IP and last seen time, but only the privacy export reads them (`privacy/service.go:212`). Sessions end only as a side effect of a password change (`auth/manage.go:436`).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `GET /auth/sessions` lists the caller's sessions with device, IP, organization, proof and last seen, marking the current one.
- [ ] `DELETE /auth/sessions/{id}` ends one, and "Sign out everywhere else" ends all but the current.
- [ ] The profile page shows the list and the actions, and each action is audited.
- [ ] `make openapi` is regenerated.

## Tests

- **Integration:** list, end one, end the others, and refuse another person's session (not found).
- **Browser:** sign in twice, end the other session from the profile, and see it signed out.

issues.title: Provision and deprovision people and groups through SCIM
issues.body:
## User story

As an IT administrator, I want people who leave the company removed from Armature when they leave the identity provider, not at their next sign-in, which never comes.

## What happens today

There is no SCIM code. Groups from the provider are replaced at each sign-in ("Groups can come from the identity provider"), so someone who never signs in again keeps their membership, their roles and their API tokens.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A SCIM 2.0 endpoint per organization (Users and Groups: create, update, deactivate, delete), authenticated by a bearer token an administrator makes and can rotate.
- [ ] Deactivating a user ends their sessions and tokens, as the administrator's switch-off does.
- [ ] Group membership maps to roles the way sign-in groups already do.
- [ ] Every change is audited, and the decisions record how SCIM and sign-in groups agree.

## Tests

- **Integration:**
  - the SCIM user and group flows;
  - a refusal without the token;
  - deactivation ends sessions and tokens;
  - RLS through raw SQL.

issues.title: Restore an archived project from the projects list and from its settings
issues.body:
## User story

As an administrator who archived a project by mistake, I want to bring it back from the UI.

## What happens today

`POST /projects/{projectKey}/restore` (`restoreProject`) has no caller in `web/src`. `routes/projects.tsx:108` renders the row menu only when `admin && !archived`, so archived rows have no actions at all. The archive confirm says "nothing is deleted, and it can be shown again", and the decision "Destructive actions confirm with the noun; undoable ones toast with Undo" applies, but the toast has no Undo.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Archived rows in the list (with Show archived on) offer Restore to administrators.
- [ ] An archived project's settings page offers Restore.
- [ ] The archive toast has Undo, which restores.

## Tests

- **Vitest:** the menu on an archived row, and the Undo.
- **Browser:** archive, undo, archive, restore from the list.

issues.title: Edit and delete your own comments, and edit a work log entry
issues.body:
## User story

As someone who made a typo in a comment, or logged 8 h instead of 0.8 h, I want to fix it in place.

## What happens today

- `PATCH` and `DELETE /issues/{issueKey}/comments/{commentID}` exist but have no caller in `web/src`.
- `CommentItem` (`features/issues/IssueActivity.tsx:46-65`) has no actions, yet it shows "edited" from `comment.editedAt`.
- `useUpdateWorklog` (`api/issues.ts:413-419`, `PATCH /worklogs/{id}`) is unused. Work log rows offer only Remove (`features/time/TimeTracking.tsx:157-161`).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A comment's author sees Edit and Delete on it. Delete confirms. Administrators can delete where the API lets them.
- [ ] A work log row offers Edit for its duration, day and note.
- [ ] Internal notes stay internal when edited.

## Tests

- **Vitest:** the actions show only for the author, and an edit saves.
- **Browser:** edit a comment and see "edited"; edit a work log and see the total change.

issues.title: Change an issue's type from the issue page
issues.body:
## User story

As someone who filed a Task that turns out to be a Bug, I want to change its type without cloning or moving it.

## What happens today

`UpdateIssueRequest` in `api/openapi.json` has `typeId`, and the server applies it (`issue/update.go:163`, `applyType`). The client's `UpdateIssueInput` (`web/src/api/issues.ts:343-354`) has no `typeId`, and the only type picker is in `CreateIssueDialog.tsx:123`.

This depends on #85 being fixed first: today a type change into another workflow resets the status without a record.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The issue's facts show its type as a field that can be changed, offering only the types at the same hierarchy level.
- [ ] When the new workflow lacks the current status, the person is told which status the issue will land in, or asked to choose.
- [ ] The server's refusal is shown as its sentence.

## Tests

- **Vitest:** the picker's choices and the refusal.
- **Browser:** change a Task to a Bug and see the history entry.

issues.title: The browser suite isolates scenarios without an organization each
issues.body:
## User story

As someone removing organizations from Armature (epic #208), I want the browser suite to keep its scenarios apart without each one signing up an organization of its own. Then every later step can land without breaking the suite.

## What happens today

- 182 of 185 scenarios start with `signUp` (`e2e/helpers.mjs:223-237`), which posts `/auth/signup` with `orgName`. Each scenario becomes the owner of an empty organization, and that organization is its sandbox. `README.md:245-247` and `e2e/runner.mjs:62-63` say so.
- Project keys come from the project name and are unique only within an organization. "Helpdesk" (HELP) is created 9 times, and "Tracked", "Read only", "Moving", "IT desk" and "Drawn" twice each.
- About ten scenarios change settings that would be installation-wide once organizations are gone. In one shared installation they would break the scenarios running beside them:
  - `accounts.mjs:240` requires a second factor for everyone, which holds every other session.
  - `themes.mjs:152` sets the default theme.
  - `dashboards.mjs:44-78` and `workflows.mjs:182-272` change the default workflow.
  - `access.mjs:148,241` sets the single sign-on provider and adds a role.
  - `holidays.mjs:38,72` sets the default calendar.
  - `organization.mjs:130` adds a field to every project.
  - `issue-details.mjs:258` renames a global label.
  - `work.mjs:110` adds a webhook that hears every event.
- The runner (`e2e/runner.mjs:65-99`) has a single queue shared by four browsers.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **One administrator per run.** A run sets up the installation's administrator once: by the first sign-up on an empty stack, or by signing in when it already exists. The helpers know its credentials.
- [ ] **`signUp` makes a new person.** The administrator creates the account (`POST /users`) with the role the scenario asks for, and the scenario signs in as it. Scenarios that administer something ask for an administrator explicitly.
- [ ] **Unique project keys.** `createProject` always passes a unique key, and scenarios read the key back rather than assume it.
- [ ] **A serial lane.** `serialScenario(name, fn)` registers a scenario that runs after the parallel pool, with one browser. Every scenario listed above is serial and puts back what it changed.
- [ ] **A guard.** A scenario that changes an installation-wide setting from the parallel pool is refused, by a check like `backend/test/parallel_test.go`'s or by a reviewed list that the runner enforces.
- [ ] **Docs.** README "Testing" and CLAUDE.md say how a scenario stays isolated.
- [ ] This lands before the sign-up change, and works both with organizations (today) and without them.

## Tests

- Two full runs in a row on the same stack, both green.
- One run with the parallel pool shuffled, to show no scenario depends on another.

Depends on: nothing. This is the first step.

issues.title: One installation: the organization is created at install, and an upgrade with several is refused
issues.body:
## User story

As the operator of an Armature installation, I want it to be one tracker with one set of people and settings, created when it is installed. Then nobody has to found an organization before they can work.

Part of epic #208.

## What happens today

- Every sign-up creates an organization (`auth.Signup`, `backend/internal/auth/service.go:61-208`, bootstrapped by `bootstrap.Org` at `backend/internal/bootstrap/bootstrap.go:73`). One installation can therefore hold any number of organizations.
- Installation-wide settings live on the `org` row: `default_theme_id` (00902), `second_factor` (00928), `automation_user_id` (00033) and the unused `settings`.
- A person can be signed in with no organization at all:
  - `passwordPrincipal` leaves `Org` nil (`backend/internal/auth/login.go:95-120`);
  - `requireOrg` then answers `no_organization` (`backend/internal/httpapi/middleware.go:438-453`);
  - every `require*Perm` repeats `p.InOrg()`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Upgrade guard.** A migration refuses to run when `org` holds more than one row. Its message names the organizations and says to delete the extra ones with the previous release first. There is no automatic merge, and the CHANGELOG has an upgrade note.
- [ ] **One organization at first start.** An empty installation gets its organization through `bootstrap.Org`, named by `ARMATURE_NAME` (default "Armature"). It is documented in the README variables table, which `config/documented_test.go` checks. Sign-up no longer creates an organization.
- [ ] **`installation` service.** A new `installation` service reads and writes the name and the settings now on `org`. Every installation-wide setting goes through it.
- [ ] **Everyone is in it.** Every signed-in principal is in the installation's organization.
  - `requireOrg`, the `no_organization` error, the `InOrg()` checks and the nil-organization paths go.
  - Someone without a membership cannot sign in. They are told "Your account has been switched off. Ask an administrator."
- [ ] **Tenant plumbing unchanged.** The backend still carries the tenant per session and per event, so `org_id` and row security keep working. The integration harness may still create extra organizations for isolation until the integration-suite ticket.
- [ ] **Decisions.** `docs/decisions.md` records the rule.

## Tests

- **Integration:**
  - the migration refuses two organizations and passes with one or none;
  - a first start creates exactly one;
  - a principal always has the organization;
  - someone without a membership is refused with the sentence.

Depends on: #209.

issues.title: Accounts without organizations: sign-up, invitations, members, owners
issues.body:
## User story

As the administrator of an Armature installation, I want accounts to belong to the installation. I set it up with the first sign-up and let people in by invitation, single sign-on or by creating them. No organization name to make up, no "member of another organization" rules.

Part of epic #208.

## What happens today

- **Sign-up** asks for `orgName` and `orgSlug` (`backend/internal/httpapi/auth_handlers.go:78-122`; `web/src/features/auth/AuthForms.tsx:264,304-314`; "Create your organization" at `web/src/routes/auth.tsx:97-98`). `SignupPolicy` (`backend/internal/auth/signup.go`) means "the first organization" or "any organization".
- **Invitations** name the organization, and they have a path for someone who already belongs to another one (`backend/internal/auth/tokens_admin.go:173-311`, `web/src/routes/invite.tsx:67-168`).
- **Removing a member** (`privacy.RemoveMember`, `DELETE /members/{id}`) keeps the account for the person's other organizations (`web/src/features/access/MemberList.tsx`).
- **Administrators manage only some accounts:** those that belong to no other organization (`managedSelectSQL.onlyHere`, `ErrManagedElsewhere`, `guardManaged` in `backend/internal/auth/manage.go:96-191`). `CreateLocalUser` refuses an address known elsewhere.
- **Organization-bound rules:**
  - An organization cannot lose its last owner (`soleActiveOwnerOf`, the trigger `app_user_keeps_an_owner` in 00049).
  - API tokens are bound to one organization (`backend/internal/auth/model.go:107-112`).
  - Avatars are visible only within a shared organization (`SharesOrganization`, `backend/internal/auth/profile.go:92`).
  - Account-level acts write one audit entry per organization (`auditEveryOrg`, `backend/internal/auth/recovery.go:154`).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Sign-up asks only for the person.** There is no organization name or slug.
  - On an empty installation, the first account becomes owner and administrator.
  - After that, `ARMATURE_SIGNUP` decides: `first` (the default) closes sign-up, `open` lets people sign up as plain members, and `closed` closes it.
  - The README row and the Helm values are updated.
- [ ] **Invitations** invite into the installation. The invitation page and mail name the installation, and the "already in another organization" path goes.
- [ ] **Removing a member switches the account off.** It uses the existing deactivation. "Remove from organization" goes.
- [ ] **Administrators manage every local account.** The sole-organization rules and their errors go.
- [ ] **Last owner becomes last active administrator.** The installation keeps at least one active administrator, in both the service and the trigger.
- [ ] **API tokens are the person's.** The "bound to one organization" wording goes.
- [ ] **Avatars are visible to everyone signed in.**
- [ ] **Account-level audit entries are written once.**
- [ ] **Decisions.** `docs/decisions.md` supersedes "An administrator makes a local user, and manages only what is theirs" and "The owner always administers their own organization".

## Tests

- **Integration:**
  - the first account becomes administrator, and the next follows the policy;
  - an invitation is accepted;
  - removing switches the account off;
  - the last administrator cannot be switched off, also checked straight through SQL;
  - an administrator manages any local account.
- **Vitest:** the sign-up form without an organization field.
- **Browser:**
  - sign-up on an empty stack (serial);
  - invite and accept.

Depends on: #209, #210.

issues.title: Sign-in without organizations: no switching, one identity provider, one second-factor rule
issues.body:
## User story

As someone signing in to Armature, I want to land straight in it. No organization to choose, no organization to type for single sign-on, and no switcher.

Part of epic #208.

## What happens today

- **Organization switching:**
  - `POST /auth/switch-org` (`backend/internal/httpapi/auth_handlers.go:204-228`, `auth.SwitchOrg` at `backend/internal/auth/service.go:437-472`) moves a session between organizations. It is allowed even while a session is held for second-factor setup (`backend/internal/httpapi/second_factor_handlers.go:50`).
  - After signing in, someone in several organizations is asked which one (`OrganizationChoice`, `web/src/features/auth/AuthForms.tsx:35-62,110-130`). Someone in none sees `web/src/features/shell/NoOrganization.tsx`.
  - The sidebar has an organization switcher (`web/src/features/shell/Sidebar.tsx:88-123`), and the profile lists organizations (`web/src/routes/profile.tsx:168-178`). `/auth/me` returns `organizations`.
- **Sessions and reach:**
  - Sessions record `current_org_id` and `proof_org_id`. `session_reaches` and `session_stays_home` (migration 00905) decide which organizations a single sign-on session reaches.
  - The session principal trusts other organizations with the same issuer (`backend/internal/auth/service.go:231-234`). `ErrSessionStaysHome` and `session_bound` (`backend/internal/httpapi/privacy_handlers.go:25-48`) refuse acts outside the session's organization.
- **Single sign-on** starts at `/auth/oidc/{orgSlug}/start`, and the login form asks for the organization (`AuthForms.tsx:132-185`). Each organization has its own provider.
- **The second-factor rule** lives at `/organization/second-factor` (`backend/internal/auth/secondfactor.go:302-330`). A held session is offered "Go to {org}" (`web/src/features/auth/SecondFactor.tsx:301-330`).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Switching goes.** `POST /auth/switch-org`, `OrganizationChoice`, `NoOrganization`, the sidebar switcher, the profile's organizations section, and `organizations`/`Membership` on `/auth/me` are deleted. The sidebar header shows the installation's name.
- [ ] **Sessions forget organizations.** Sessions no longer write `current_org_id` or `proof_org_id`. `session_reaches`, `session_stays_home`, the cross-organization issuer trust, `ErrSessionStaysHome` and `session_bound` go. The session's proof stays.
- [ ] **One identity provider:**
  - Sign-in starts at `/auth/oidc/start`.
  - `/auth/oidc/{orgSlug}/start` redirects there for one release.
  - The login form offers "Continue with single sign-on" without an organization field.
  - Provider settings show the new address.
- [ ] **The second-factor rule moves to `/settings/second-factor`.** It reads "for administrators" or "for everyone", and the "another organization" offers and messages go.
- [ ] **Docs.** `make openapi` is regenerated. `docs/decisions.md` supersedes "A sign-in reaches what its proof vouches for", and SECURITY.md's Session provenance row is updated.

## Tests

- **Integration:**
  - sign-in lands in the installation;
  - single sign-on starts at the new address, and the old one redirects;
  - the second-factor rule works at its new path;
  - a held session can still sign out and enrol.
- **Vitest:** login without a choice; the sidebar without a switcher.
- **Browser:** the accounts, access and invitations scenarios.

Depends on: #210, #211.

issues.title: Delete organization lifecycle: creating, demo organizations, deleting
issues.body:
## User story

As the administrator of an Armature installation, I want no buttons that make or delete organizations. There is one installation, and its settings page is about that installation.

Part of epic #208.

## What happens today

- **Demo organizations.** `POST /organizations/demo` (`backend/internal/httpapi/auth_handlers.go:230-264`) makes a demo organization and switches into it, through `auth.CreateOrganization` (`backend/internal/auth/service.go:392-435`) and `demo.Factory` (`backend/internal/demo/factory.go`).
- **Deleting an organization.** `DELETE /organization` (`backend/internal/httpapi/privacy_handlers.go:98-112`, `backend/internal/privacy/organization.go`) deletes an organization and everything in it.
- **The settings page.** `/settings/organization` (`web/src/routes/organization.tsx`) shows the name and slug, "Create a demo organization" and the delete dialog.
- **The `org.created` event.** `TopicOrgCreated` (`backend/internal/events/events.go:25,62`) announces new organizations.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **The organization endpoints go.** `POST /organizations/demo`, `auth.CreateOrganization`, `DELETE /organization`, `privacy.DeleteOrganization` and `TopicOrgCreated` are deleted.
- [ ] **The demo stays available.** `demo.Factory` stays for the seed. An administrator action "Add the demo project" loads it into the installation.
- [ ] **An Installation page.** The organization settings page becomes "Installation", which shows and renames the installation's name and nothing about creating or deleting.
- [ ] **Organization-lifecycle tests go:**
  - browser: `e2e/scenarios/organization-delete.mjs`, `organization.mjs:162`, `invitations.mjs:114`, `projects.mjs:170`;
  - integration: `organization_delete_test.go`, `demo_test.go`, `TestOrgSwitching`;
  - the takeover and single-sign-on-reach tests are rewritten for one installation.
- [ ] **Docs.** `docs/privacy.md` loses "An organization letting a member go" and organization deletion. `make openapi` is regenerated.

## Tests

- **Integration:** the demo project action fills the installation.
- **Vitest:** the Installation page.
- **Browser:** renaming the installation shows in the sidebar (serial).

Depends on: #210, #212.

issues.title: The service desk without an organization slug
issues.body:
## User story

As a customer of a service desk, I want the desk's address to name the desk, not an organization slug I have never heard of.

Part of epic #208.

## What happens today

- **Desk addresses.** The public desk lives at `/desk/{orgSlug}`, with `/desk/{orgSlug}/codes` and `/desk/{orgSlug}/sessions` (`backend/internal/httpapi/router.go:62-64`, `deskBySlug` at `backend/internal/httpapi/portal_entry_handlers.go:185-195`).
  - The web route is `web/src/routes/desk-entry.tsx` (`/desk/$orgSlug`).
  - The address shown to agents comes from `web/src/features/desk/DeskExtras.tsx:293-295`.
- **Portal codes and doors.** These bind the organization (`codeDigest(orgID, ...)`, `desksTrust`, `OpenDoors` in `backend/internal/auth/portal.go:77-137`). Code mail, the satisfaction page (`web/src/routes/rate.tsx`) and the portal header name the organization.
- **Inbound mail.** It resolves a project key across organizations and has an "ambiguous" outcome (`backend/internal/desk/inbound.go:280-343`).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **The desk lives at `/desk?desk=KEY`.** Its codes and sessions follow. The old `/desk/{orgSlug}` addresses redirect for one release.
- [ ] **The web follows.** The web route and the address shown to agents use the new form.
- [ ] **Portal codes and doors.** Codes and open doors no longer carry the organization.
- [ ] **Customer-facing text.** Code mail, the satisfaction page and the portal header name the installation or the desk.
- [ ] **Inbound mail.** The "ambiguous across organizations" outcome goes.
- [ ] **OpenAPI.** `make openapi` is regenerated.

## Tests

- **Integration:**
  - desk entry, code and session at the new address, and the redirect from the old one;
  - inbound mail reaches the desk.
- **Browser:** `desk.mjs` and `desk-mail.mjs` without `orgSlug`.

Depends on: #210.

issues.title: Say "everyone" instead of "the organization" in the product and the API
issues.body:
## User story

As someone using Armature, I want the words on screen to match what there is: settings that apply to every project, not to an "organization" I never chose.

Part of epic #208.

## What happens today

- **UI strings.** About 87 strings in 72 files under `web/src` say "organization". Most of them mean "all projects" or "everyone", for example:
  - "Follow the organization" (`web/src/features/workflows/ProjectWorkflows.tsx`, `web/src/features/arrange/ArrangementEditor.tsx:76`)
  - "Share with the organization" (`web/src/routes/themes.tsx`)
  - "Only over the whole organization" (`web/src/features/access/RoleMatrix.tsx`)
  - "Rules across every project of {org}" (`web/src/routes/automation.tsx:56`)
- **Guide and permission label.** The guide catalogue (`web/src/features/guide/catalogue.ts:81-116`) and the permission label "Administer the organization" (`backend/internal/perm/definitions.go:85`) use the same word.
- **OpenAPI.** It has an "organization" tag and summaries (`backend/internal/httpapi/openapi_operations.go`).
- **Theme source.** The theme source value `"organization"` (`web/src/api/themes.ts:29`, `backend/internal/theme/service.go:78`) names where a default theme comes from.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **UI copy and help** say "everyone", "all projects" or "Armature", whichever fits each place. The only exception is the Installation page.
- [ ] **The permission label** reads "Administer Armature". Its key `org.administer` stays, because stored role grants use it.
- [ ] **The theme source `"organization"`** becomes `"everyone"` in the API and the client.
- [ ] **OpenAPI tags and summaries** are updated, and `make openapi` is regenerated.
- [ ] **`data-*` hooks** that tests or users rely on stay.

## Tests

- **Vitest and browser:** selectors that read copy are updated.
- **A check:** a test refuses the word "organization" in UI strings outside the Installation page and the tests.

Depends on: #211, #212, #213, #214.

issues.title: Docs, seed and deployment for one installation
issues.body:
## User story

As someone installing or upgrading Armature, I want the README, the deployment files, the seed and the decisions to describe one installation. Then nothing tells me about organizations that no longer exist.

Part of epic #208.

## What happens today

- **The seed** signs up "Demo Company" with slug `demo` and works inside that organization (`backend/cmd/seed/main.go:99-180`).
- **Helm** describes sign-up per organization and seeds "the demo organization":
  - `deploy/charts/armature/values.yaml:209-213`
  - `values-demo.yaml:8,19-23`
  - `templates/NOTES.txt:20`
- **README:**
  - line 17 calls Armature multi-tenant;
  - lines 37-45 describe the demo organization;
  - lines 225-255 base test isolation on organizations;
  - lines 331-333 cover sessions reaching organizations;
  - the `ARMATURE_SIGNUP` row needs updating.
- **SECURITY.md** has Tenancy and Session provenance rows.
- **`docs/privacy.md`** and **`docs/design/*`** describe organizations.
- **`docs/decisions.md`** has about 85 mentions. The tenancy-facing entries start at lines 1470, 1537, 1559, 1617 and 1704.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **The seed** fills the installation with the demo project and people.
- [ ] **Helm and compose** carry `ARMATURE_NAME` and the new sign-up wording, and `NOTES.txt` says what was seeded.
- [ ] **README, SECURITY.md, `docs/privacy.md` and `docs/design/*`** describe one installation.
- [ ] **`docs/decisions.md`** gains "One installation is one team's tracker":
  - it supersedes the tenancy-facing entries;
  - it says why several organizations are refused rather than merged;
  - it explains that `org_id` and row security stay internally until the schema ticket.
- [ ] **The CHANGELOG** has upgrade notes:
  - an installation with several organizations is refused;
  - the old single sign-on and desk addresses redirect for one release;
  - `ARMATURE_NAME`.

## Tests

- `config/documented_test.go` passes with `ARMATURE_NAME`.
- `make up` followed by the seed gives a working demo installation.
- The browser screenshots script runs.

Depends on: #210, #211, #212, #213, #214, #215.

issues.title: The integration suite isolates tests without an organization each
issues.body:
## User story

As someone working on Armature, I want the integration suite to keep its tests apart and parallel without giving each test an organization of its own. Then the schema can lose `org_id`.

Part of epic #208.

## What happens today

- 344 integration tests create organizations through `newWorkspace`, `makeOrg` or `signup` (`backend/test/harness_test.go:82,208,270`; `apiclient_test.go:282`). README lines 236-241 say each parallel test "works in organizations of its own".
- 91 tests create two or more organizations. Some exist only to prove tenant isolation:
  - `tenant_isolation_test.go`, `security_test.go:16` and `issue_isolation_test.go`;
  - the per-feature isolation tests: boards, fields, git, hierarchy, old keys, page links, digests, token projects, webhooks, workflow schemes and join requests.
- `backend/test/parallel_test.go:35-61` justifies some sequential tests by passes "over every organization".

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Unique names, one organization.** Tests isolate themselves by unique people, projects and names inside the one organization. `newWorkspace` and `makeOrg` give way to helpers that make a project and people.
- [ ] **Isolation-only tests go.** Tests that prove only isolation between organizations are deleted. Where a project wall covers the same ground, that test is kept or written.
- [ ] **Shared settings run alone.** Tests that change installation-wide settings join `parallel_test.go`'s sequential list, each with its reason.
- [ ] **Docs.** README "Testing" and CLAUDE.md describe the new isolation.

## Tests

- The suite is green and still parallel. The wall-clock time is reported against today's 45 to 55s.
- Five green runs in a row.

Depends on: #210, #211, #212, #213, #214, #215, #216.

issues.title: Drop org_id and the tenant layer from the schema
issues.body:
## User story

As someone working on Armature, I want the schema and the code to stop carrying an organization that is always the same. Then queries, triggers and new features no longer pay for multi-tenancy.

Part of epic #208.

## What happens today

- **Schema:**
  - 94 of 101 tables carry `org_id`.
  - Each has a `_tenant_isolation` and an `_admin_bypass` policy (190 in total), under forced row security. Every policy is pure tenant isolation; project walls, portal scoping and customer rules live in Go and in triggers.
  - About 30 unique indexes and primary keys include `org_id`, for example `project (org_id, key)`. So do the `absence_no_overlap` exclusion and the `role_assignment` to `org_role` foreign key.
  - 36 trigger functions refer to the organization. Some mix tenant checks with project, customer or owner rules that must stay: `issue_sprint_guard`, `team_member_guard`, `absence_guard`, `saved_filter_share_guard`, `role_assignment_guard`, `app_user_keeps_an_owner` and others.
- **Go:**
  - `internal/tenant`, `db.inTx`'s `set_config('app.org_id')` and `ErrNoTenant`.
  - About 129 INSERT column lists with `org_id`, 93 `current_org_id()` uses, 17 `ON CONFLICT (org_id, ...)` clauses and 46 explicit `org_id` filters.
  - 8 worker loops run once per organization: retention, sprint and flow snapshots, digest, subscriptions, SLA watch, automation schedules, webhooks.
  - `events.Event.OrgID` and the Redis stream field; webhook payloads carry `orgId`.
- **Tables:** `org`, `org_member` and `org_role` hold what becomes installation settings and per-person roles.

## Acceptance criteria

The work goes in this order, because Postgres drops dependent objects silently: dropping a column drops its indexes and policies, and trigger bodies fail only at runtime.

- [ ] **1. Policies.** Decide whether any row security remains, for example project walls, and record it in `docs/decisions.md`. Replace or drop the tenant policies, the admin bypass policies and FORCE. Rewrite `rls_bypass_test`, `backfill_rls_test` and `owner_migrate_test`.
- [ ] **2. Constraints.** Recreate every unique index, primary key, exclusion and foreign key that includes `org_id` without it, before the column goes. Project keys become globally unique.
- [ ] **3. Triggers.** Rewrite all 36 trigger functions. Keep their project, customer and owner rules, and drop the "cannot cross organizations" parts.
- [ ] **4. Go.** Remove `org_id` from inserts, conflicts and filters. Delete `internal/tenant` and the tenant setting. Run the worker loops once. Remove `Event.OrgID` and the stream field. Drop `orgId` from webhook payloads; this is a documented contract change, so the CHANGELOG says so.
- [ ] **5. Tables.** `org` becomes an `installation` settings row, `org_member` becomes a role on `app_user`, and `org_role` becomes `role`. Decide whether the `armature_admin` role split stays.
- [ ] **6. Upgrade.** The upgrade note says to drain the outbox and the event stream before migrating.

## Tests

- The full suite on all four layers.
- A migration test that starts from a populated one-organization database and checks every row survives.
- A check that no table, column or function mentions `org_id` or `current_org_id`.

Depends on: #210, #211, #212, #213, #214, #215, #216, #217.

issues.title: Say what kind of thing a remote link is
issues.body:
## User story

As somebody reading an issue, I want the requirements that trace to it shown apart from the wiki pages about it, so that I can tell at a glance what the issue implements from what merely documents it.

## Context

Exciter, the requirements tool, traces requirements to Armature issues and puts a remote link on each issue with `source: "Exciter"`, as Stator does for pages with `source: "Stator"`. The Pages panel lists every remote link of an issue as one list, so requirements sit among pages, told apart only by their source text.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `RemoteLinkRequest`, `RemoteLink` and the `issue.remote_link.added` / `issue.remote_link.removed` payloads carry a `relation` (or `kind`), such as `page` or `requirement`; a link sent without one is `page`, so existing callers keep working
- [ ] The issue page groups remote links by it, under a heading each (Pages, Requirements)
- [ ] `api/openapi.json` describes the field

A smaller alternative, if a new field is not wanted: the panel groups remote links by `source` under a heading each.

## Tests

Unit: the default for links without a relation. Integration: a link put with `requirement` reads back with it. Playwright: the issue page shows a requirement under its own heading.

## Implementation

`internal/issue/remotelinks.go`, migration on `issue_remote_link`, `web/src/features/issues/PagesPanel.tsx`.

Asked for by Cloudster1/Exciter#27; Exciter works without it and would send `requirement` once it exists.

issues.title: Name the status categories in transition webhook payloads
issues.body:
## User story

As an integrator receiving webhooks, I want a transition's payload to name the status categories it moved between, so that I can keep an issue's category without asking for the issue again.

## Context

`issue.transitioned` carries `fromStatus` and `toStatus` by name but not their categories. Exciter stores the status category of every issue a requirement traces to, for everyone, so coverage counts it without asking Armature as each reader. A webhook has no person to ask as, so today Exciter can only mark the stored category stale until somebody reads the issue.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `issue.transitioned` payloads carry `fromStatusCategory` and `toStatusCategory` (`todo`, `in_progress`, `done`) beside `fromStatus` and `toStatus`
- [ ] The webhook topics documentation names the new fields

## Tests

Unit: the payload a transition emits carries both categories.

## Implementation

`internal/issue/transition.go`, where the payload is built.

Asked for by Cloudster1/Exciter#29; Exciter works without it and stores the category at once when it is there.

issues.title: Add a suite demo filled with the issues of Armature, Exciter and Stator
issues.body:
## User story

As someone trying Armature together with Exciter and Stator, I want a demo whose issues are the suite's own development history, so that I see the three tools working on real, linked content rather than invented examples.

Part of one suite demo: Armature holds the issues, Stator the documentation (praetorianer777/Stator#457) and Exciter the requirements (Cloudster1/Exciter#270), and Exciter traces between them.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Adding it:** an administrator adds the suite demo once, from Settings > Installation beside "Add the demo project", and `make seed` adds it too. It is refused when one of its keys is taken.
- [ ] **Projects:** three projects, `ARM`, `EXC` and `STA`, hold the GitHub issues of `Cloudster1/Armature`, `Cloudster1/Exciter` and `praetorianer777/Stator`. Pull requests are left out.
- [ ] **Issues:** each keeps its GitHub number as its key (`EXC-261` is Exciter issue #261), its title, its Markdown body as a document, its labels and its milestone. Closed issues are done, with the date they closed.
- [ ] **Dependencies:** "Depends on" references become blocking links, also across projects (`Cloudster1/Exciter#59` in an Armature issue links to `EXC-59`).
- [ ] **People:** no GitHub login or email address is copied. Reporters and assignees are the seed's demo people.
- [ ] **Snapshot:** the content comes from a snapshot in the repository, so adding the demo needs no network. `make demo-snapshot` refreshes it with `gh` and records the date and commit of each repository.
- [ ] **Partners:** once Exciter and Stator add their part, the issues show their requirements and pages as remote links. Those tools push the links; Armature needs nothing new for that.

## Tests

- Go unit: the snapshot maps to issues (keys, states, closing dates, labels, milestones, people, "Depends on" links).
- Integration: add the demo; a second add and a taken key are refused; each project holds as many issues as its snapshot; a cross-project blocking link exists.
- Browser: add the demo from Settings, open `EXC-261` and see its blocking link, with the accessibility check.

## Implementation

- Beside `backend/internal/demo`, through `issue.ImportInput` with `KeyNum` for the GitHub number and `ExternalKey` set to the issue URL, so that a renewed snapshot updates the issues instead of copying them.
- One JSON file per repository; the keys join `demo.Keys` so the two demos never clash.
- A decision in `docs/decisions.md`: why a snapshot and not a live import from GitHub.

Depends on: nothing.

issues.title: List mcp@1 in /meta
issues.body:
## User story

As a partner tool such as Rotor, we want Armature to say it offers MCP, so we read it by name before acting in it as a person.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `GET /api/v1/meta` lists `mcp@1`: MCP at `POST /api/v1/mcp`, taking the tokens of `oauth.partner-tokens@1`
- [ ] The capability test holds it to the route table
- [ ] `docs/integration.md` describes it, as Exciter's does

## Tests

Unit: the capability tests.

## Implementation

- One entry in `integrationCapabilities` (`backend/internal/httpapi/capabilities.go`), operation `POST /mcp`, promising what Exciter's `mcp@1` promises.

## Depends on

- Nothing. Cloudster1/Rotor#45 waits on it.
